# datagoodr

> Rule-based data governance for the CSV world. Gooder data means gooder
> research.

`datagoodr` documents, types, and profiles research datasets — turning a
bare CSV into a governed, self-describing data asset and a readable
Research Guide.

## The problem: ungoverned data corrupts science and analytics

A CSV carries no schema. Whether `47401` is a ZIP code, a county FIPS,
or a count is invisible — so every tool that opens the file guesses, and
they guess differently. A leading zero is dropped, a date is parsed in
the wrong order, a coded category is averaged as if it were a number.
These are not edge cases; they are the daily reality of applied research
and organizational analytics, and they quietly corrupt findings long
before anyone notices.

The discipline that prevents this — **data governance**: protecting,
refining, and responsibly sharing data assets — has been a core concern
of information systems for decades. But it has become urgent in
statistics and the social sciences, where the creation and sharing of
new data sources has grown exponentially while governance practice has
not kept pace. The usual answer is an enterprise data-governance system:
a heavyweight platform with complex schemas, unfamiliar data-type
ontologies, and a price tag and staffing model that put it out of reach
for most labs, analysts, and academics. Governance that demands all of
that simply fails to meet most people where they are.

**datagoodr is a feasible alternative.** It is organized around familiar
data types and **CSV files** — the default currency of the scientific
world and organizational analysts — and around a single, legible
artifact anyone can edit in a spreadsheet. Governance becomes a set of
named rules attached to your data, not a platform you have to adopt.

## How it works

![datagoodr workflow](reference/figures/workflow.svg)

At the center is the **Data Governance File (DGF)**: a table with one
row per variable that is both a *governed data dictionary* and the
*control center* for the whole workflow.
[`create_dgf()`](https://urbaninstitute.github.io/datagoodr/reference/create_dgf.md)
profiles every column and types it (using the
[formex](https://lecy.github.io/formex/) detection engine); you curate
the result in a spreadsheet — adding labels, definitions, and corrected
types; and the DGF then drives two outputs:

- **a stabilized Governed CSV**
  ([`stabilize_data()`](https://urbaninstitute.github.io/datagoodr/reference/stabilize_data.md))
  that imports to the correct type where possible, and *safely* —
  without data loss — where not; and
- **a Research Guide**
  ([`create_rg()`](https://urbaninstitute.github.io/datagoodr/reference/create_rg.md)):
  a rendered data profile with a visual tuned to each column’s type.

As the data changes,
[`update_dgf()`](https://urbaninstitute.github.io/datagoodr/reference/update_dgf.md)
re-profiles it while preserving everything you curated.

> **Acronyms.** **DGF** = Data Governance File · **RG** = Research
> Guide.

## Installation

``` r

# datagoodr depends on the formex detection engine
remotes::install_github("lecy/formex")
remotes::install_github("UrbanInstitute/datagoodr")
```

## Documentation

The user guide is being built out as a set of vignettes (Getting
Started, the workflow, rule-based governance, stabilizing datasets, data
profiling, research guides, and documentation). Start with **Rule-Based
Data Governance** and **Guessing Data Types** in the Articles section of
the package website, pending the full set.

## Development plan and current state

datagoodr is under active development. The current cycle **reintegrated
the type-detection layer into [formex](https://github.com/lecy/formex)**
and adopted formex’s v7 ontology, so datagoodr is now cleanly *the
workflow* and formex is *the engine*.

**Implemented**

- **Detection extracted to formex.** The ~80 `is_*` detectors, the
  ontology, and `guess_data_type()` now live in formex, which datagoodr
  imports. datagoodr keeps profiling, the DGF, review/override,
  stabilization, and rendering.
- **A clearer rule vocabulary.** Ingest rules were renamed `as_*` →
  `read_*` (the name now states the format a rule *reads*), with
  deprecated shims.
- **Dual-modality typing.**
  [`create_dgf()`](https://urbaninstitute.github.io/datagoodr/reference/create_dgf.md)
  reads both of formex’s predictions (the ontology route and the legacy
  detectors) with a storage-safety gate that protects zero-padded keys
  (FIPS, ZIP, EIN) from being coerced to numbers.
- **The v7 two-axis DGF.** Each column carries a machine `guess_*` leaf
  (`format_style` + `unit_type`), a human-editable `desired_*` target
  form, and a suggested **`stabilizer`** — a
  `read :: [convert] :: write` plan — previewed in `stable_first5`.
- **Executable stabilization.** `stabilize_data(use_v7 = TRUE)` runs
  those plans to produce the governed CSV; legacy rules still take
  precedence.
- **Profiling + rendering.** Universal quality metrics (distinct,
  missingness, zeros, infinities, duplication) plus type-specific
  profiles, rendered as a Research Guide with per-type visuals
  (histogram, treemap, calendar heat-map, boolean bar, word cloud).

**In progress / planned**

- The full user-guide vignette set (see
  `dev/vignette-user-guide-plan.md`).
- Porting the render engine off the legacy
  `desired_data_type`/`desired_data_class` columns onto the v7 axes.
- Additional profile metrics (e.g. entropy / categorical balance) under
  consideration.

Planning notes and design rationale live in `dev/`
(`formex-reintegration-plan.md`, `schema-simplification-plan.md`,
`v7-dgf-integration-plan.md`).

# Package index

  : Abbreviate numbers for compact, uniform axis/graphic labels

  : Draw a compact horizontal bar plot with consistent bar geometry
